thread:
Maya: heads up — hitting lost spans on fast shutdown in a few customer apps. python + gunicorn/uvicorn combo, spans just never make it to otlp collector.
Kevin: ugh. is the app process exiting before the exporter flush? check SIGTERM handler ordering.
Maya: yep looks like gunicorn master sends SIGTERM -> workers shutdown quickly. we call tracer.shutdown() but background sender sometimes blocked on network and process exits.
Igor: common. python stdlib atexit / GC finalizers unreliable under fork. we saw this with our old sdk shim.
Sam: what about forcing sync export with a short timeout in shutdown path? e.g. tracer.shutdown(timeout=2000) blocking on export flush.
Maya: tried blocking but gunicorn kills after 2s; some spans are still buffered. Also some frameworks call sys.exit which bypasses cleanup.
Elena: Rust side had similar: tokio runtime drop ordering meant exporter future got canceled. We added an explicit async close() that returns when queue drained. That helped.
Kevin: for go, we push a non-blocking flush + draining channel with context deadline. but if the host restarts container hard, you're out of luck. we mitigated with local persistent queue for a few seconds.
Sam: proposal: SDK surface should be explicit and cross-language: init(...), flush(timeout_ms), shutdown(timeout_ms) and SDK ensures best-effort background drain but caller should call shutdown on graceful termination. Add env var REDWOOD_OTEL_GRACE_PERIOD to tune.
Igor: +1 but need clear docs for common deployment patterns: gunicorn, uwsgi, systemd, k8s preStop hook. Otherwise users won't do it.
Maya: also found python issue: uvicorn's lifespan context exits before background threads finish. putting tracer.shutdown() inside lifespan exit works. adding to docs is OK but we should add an auto-hook for uvicorn/gunicorn in our redwood-otel package.
Elena: auto-hooks are tricky cross-lang. Maybe provide small opinionated helpers: redwood_otel.instrument_uvicorn(app) and redwood_otel.instrument_gunicorn_worker() that wire proper signal handlers.
Kevin: beware of double-handling signals for customers who already handle them. helpers should be opt-in.
Sam: another edge: exporter backpressure — when OTLP gRPC endpoint is slow, SDK queues grow and memory spikes. We need bounded queue + reject/drop policy + observable metric so console can show exporter backlog and trigger alerts/quotas.
Maya: yes, console dashboard needs a per-service exporter_queue_size, drops_count, last_flush_time. for rollouts, we can gate the new bounded-queue behavior behind a config flag so we can do canary.
Igor: retention/ingest side: if SDK retries keep creating duplicates, downstream dedup becomes messy. We should ensure idempotency via span ids + stable resource tags (tenant id).
Sam: sampling: make sampling decision deterministic early (at api entry) and attach to span attr so router/exporter can decide per-tenant retention. that reduces downstream cost.
Elena: for Rust/Python/Go SDKs we should expose the same envs and config keys: REDWOOD_OTEL_SAMPLING, REDWOOD_OTEL_FLUSH_MS, REDWOOD_OTEL_QUEUE_MAX. keeps rollout simpler.
Kevin: ops-bot: FYI we created a short-lived k8s job to test forced restarts; logs at https://internal/redwood/logs/2123456789.
ops-bot: deploy detected: canary redwood-otel-helper v0.2.1 -> staging (maya).
Maya: thanks. next steps: 1) add shutdown+flush API spec for all langs, 2) docs for k8s/gunicorn/uvicorn, 3) instrumented helpers (opt-in) for python, 4) bounded queue + exporter metrics and config flags for rollout.
Igor: I'll draft the spec for Rust & integration tests for tokio shutdown ordering.
Kevin: I'll do Go + bounded queue impl and Prometheus metrics.
Sam: I'll prototype a minimal python helper that uses lifecycle events and exposes a CLI entrypoint to wrap gunicorn.
Elena: I'll add sampling determinism doc and the env var list.
Maya: cool — aim to canary the queue + helper behind feature flag next week. :thumbsup:
Kevin: +1
Sam: +1
Igor: +1
Elena: +1
